forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Hertfordshire pension fund rebalances £3bn portfolio to meet new legal deadline
news_drafts.lead: Hertfordshire's Local Government Pension Scheme has established new investment allocations across nine asset classes to comply with regulations introduced by the Pension Schemes Act 2026. The revised Investment Strategy Statement must be published by 31 March 2027, with the Pensions Committee to approve a draft on 23 October and final approval targeted for February 2027. The fund has set strategic ranges for listed equities at 34.5 per cent, credit at 16.5 per cent, and UK government bonds at 13.5 per cent, with defined rebalancing ranges to maintain risk controls while minimising transaction costs. Officers are also recommending a flexible local investment allocation of 0 to 5 per cent, working with the Border to Coast investment pool, which expects to deploy funds from December 2026. However, Hertfordshire's pending Local Government Reorganisation has made it impossible to resolve key implementation questions about return targets, local investment priorities and impact measurement, deferring those decisions pending clarity on the council's future structure.

findings.paper_title: 07a 261023 Appendix A Hertfordshire - Performance Report to 30 June 2026_Public
findings.headline: Total Fund market value rose from £7,047.3M to £7,451.7M in the quarter, with investment growth of £398.5M.
findings.detail: The paper shows net cashflow of £5.8M and investment growth of £398.5M across the Fund in the quarter. Growth assets rose to £2,896.3M and bonds to £1,840.2M.
findings.matters: The size of the quarterly gain against the modest net cashflow is the headline driver of funding-level movements for employer councils.
findings.figures: Total 31/03/2026 £7,047.3M; net cashflow £5.8M; investment growth £398.5M; total 30/06/2026 £7,451.7M

findings.paper_title: 07a 261023 Appendix A Hertfordshire - Performance Report to 30 June 2026_Public
findings.headline: Equity Protection Insight mandate shows a negative market value of -£47.3M at 30 June 2026.
findings.detail: The paper reports a negative market value for the Equity Protection Insight line, after a net cashflow of £10.8M and an investment decline of £64.1M in the quarter. Its share of the Fund is shown as -0.6%.
findings.matters: A negative market value on a protection mandate is unusual and will prompt questions from anyone reviewing the Fund's derivative or hedging exposure.
findings.figures: Market value 31/03/2026 £6.0M; net cashflow £10.8M; investment decline -£64.1M; market value 30/06/2026 -£47.3M; allocation -0.6%

findings.paper_title: 07a 261023 Appendix A Hertfordshire - Performance Report to 30 June 2026_Public
findings.headline: Fund placed £247.6M into a new BCPP Investment Grade Credit mandate, with inception dated 24 June 2026.
findings.detail: The paper shows net cashflow of £247.6M into the BCPP IG Credit mandate in the quarter and a market value of £247.3M at 30 June 2026. Performance is shown only since inception.
findings.matters: A new pooled credit allocation of this size shows where a pension fund is moving its bond exposure, which is relevant to peers considering the same pool.
findings.figures: Net cashflow £247.6M; market value 30/06/2026 £247.3M; quarter return -0.4% (benchmark -0.5%)

findings.paper_title: 07a 261023 Appendix A Hertfordshire - Performance Report to 30 June 2026_Public
findings.headline: Fund's growth allocation stands at 38.9% against a 34.5% benchmark, and bonds at 24.7% against 30.0%, after a rebalance to a new strategic allocation.
findings.detail: The Committee agreed a new strategic asset allocation in Q1 2026. The Fund reduced listed equities and moved the proceeds into index-linked gilts and BCPP Investment Grade Credit. The remaining rebalancing was due in early July 2026.
findings.matters: A new strategic allocation with a scheduled completion date is a decision a finance officer elsewhere can compare against their own fund's rebalancing and risk settings.
findings.quote: The Committee agreed a new strategic asset allocation (SAA) in Q1 2026.

findings.paper_title: 07a 261023 Appendix A Hertfordshire - Performance Report to 30 June 2026_Public
findings.headline: Fund's ten-year return of 6.8% a year is reported as ahead of its 5.8% benchmark.
findings.detail: The paper says the Fund outperformed the benchmark over ten years, the one period in the table where it is ahead. Its 3-year return was behind.
findings.matters: A longer-run lead over benchmark is the kind of evidence a finance officer at another fund would use when judging whether shorter-term shortfalls are persistent.
findings.quote: The Fund’s investments have outperformed the benchmark during the ten year period.
